newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi says Italy budget shows will to be in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says Italy budget shows will to be in EMU.

text.p: Italy's tough 1997 budget to slash the public deficit shows the country's clear will to participate fully in Europe's planned single currency, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told parliament on Thursday.

He said official downwards revision of the government's deficit-GDP ratio for 1997 to three percent as a result of the measures was intended as a signal "to everyone, without a shadow of a doubt, that Italy intends to be in a united Europe, a full-fledged member of that union which our country has actively promoted since its conception".
Ciampi was presenting the budget, which aims to slash next year's public deficit by 62.5 trillion lire, to the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) at the start of its passage through parliament.
He said inflation was continuing to fall, leading to lower market interest rates, and that consumer price inflation should be below three precent by the end of the year.
A fall in real interest rates would boost the Italian economy, stimulating investment and jobs and reducing the interest burden on the public debt to manageable levels, Ciampi said.

"We have a duty to create credibility. That is the way to reduce interest rates and thus the public deficit," he told the house, where the centre-right opposition has branded the budget an "all-tax" package that will cause recession and not be enough get Italy into monetary union from its 1999 start.
